I work all day for the family, and the whole garden quietly depends on my commute.
I did not always look like this, and the change happened behind a closed door.
I started life underwater, and I still prefer the damp end of the garden.
I would rather be underground, and your vegetables are the only reason I visit.
I found the warmest square of sun in this house and I will be there until it moves.
I hear the car before anybody else and I am at the door by the time you reach it.

I sleep standing up, and I can read your mood from the way you hold the rope.

I end each day with your hair in my face.

I am what yesterday becomes once the pan is hot enough.
I arrive in a box, and the argument over the last of me starts immediately.
I was small and quiet until the heat arrived, and now I am the loudest thing in the room.
I melt in the hand that was supposed to be saving me for later.
I am racing you, and on a hot day I am winning.
I was several pieces of fruit this morning and now I arrive through a straw.
My little squares were built to hold whatever you pour over me.
I go dark on purpose and everybody thanks me for it.
I am busiest once everyone else has finished work.
I am empty six days a week and deafening on the seventh.
My curtain is the most patient thing in the building.
I am full of voices and not one of them is speaking out loud.
Everything inside me is older than everybody looking at it.
I am deafening for four minutes at a time, then silent again.
Half of us here are watching the other half, and we disagree about which half is which.
I am full of people who are all somewhere else in their heads.
My lights never go off, and nobody comes to me by choice.
I am a line of people with one counter at the end of it.
Everybody looks up at me at the same moment, then straight back down.
I only ever tell you one thing, and I have never once been wrong about it.
I looked a great deal better on the shelf where you found me.
I am always exactly one item too small.
You remember me either far too late or not at all.
I am the most important thing you own for about two hours.
I was very confident this morning and almost none of me survived the day.
I have never once folded back the way I came.
I hold the worst picture of you in existence and you carry me everywhere.
I am slower than flying, and nobody who picks me minds that.
I arrive with you and leave several days later.
I am the part of the journey nobody puts in the photographs.
I have been a hundred people's car this year and not one of them washed me.
